# 1. Survey data and exploratory analysis

This section summarizes the spatial and temporal distribution of survey observations for *`r sp_scientific`*. Biomass, biomass density, and spatial autocorrelation are examined before fitting the candidate models.

## 1.1. Observed biomass of *`r sp_scientific`*

Survey observations are mapped by year. Point size represents observed biomass (kg), while colour distinguishes presence from absence. The western and eastern English Channel are displayed separately when selected. 

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}


if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {

  plot_west <- NULL
  
  EC_sf <- vect(here("01_DATA", "shapefiles", "west7e", "west7e.shp"))%>%
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326)

 plot_west <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = EC_sf) +   
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = EC_sf, fill = NA) +        
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = data_CGFS_west, 
                     aes(x = lon, y = lat, 
                         color = factor(presence_absence), 
                         size  = totalWeightKg), 
                     alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "red", "1" = "blue"), 
                     labels = c("Absence", "Presence"), 
                     name = "Occurence") +
  scale_size_continuous(name ="Biomass (kg)") +
  facet_wrap(~ year, nrow=2) +
  labs(x=NULL, y=NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), 
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, margin = margin(t=2, b=2)))
 
 plot_west
 
}

```

## 1.3. Annual spatial autocorrelation analysis of biomass density

For each year, Moran's I is calculated to assess spatial autocorrelation in the observed biomass density data. The annual results are visualized to identify years exhibiting statistically significant spatial autocorrelation.  
The null hypothesis (H₀) assumes no spatial autocorrelation, whereas the alternative hypothesis (H₁) indicates the presence of spatial autocorrelation. Statistical significance was evaluated using a threshold of p < 0.05.
A significant positive Moran's I indicates spatial clustering of similar biomass density values, while a significant negative Moran's I indicates spatial dispersion, with neighbouring locations tending to exhibit dissimilar values. Non-significant results indicate insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis.


```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {
  p_autocorr_west <- moran_by_region$west
  p_autocorr_west
}
```

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
if (isTRUE(East_English_Channel)) {

  p_autocorr_east
  }
```

# 3. Candidate model evaluation

Candidate models are assessed using fitting diagnostics, parameter estimates, simulation-based residual checks, conditional AIC, and repeated random cross-validation.

## 3.1. Model fitting and validation status

The matrix summarizes model outcomes for each region, mesh, response, and distribution family. Models are classified as valid, failed to fit, or rejected by post-fit consistency checks.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

statuses_type <- c("models_valid", "models_sanity_failed", "models_fit_failed")

sanity_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(sanity_by_region, function(meshes_by_region, region) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(meshes_by_region, function(responses_by_mesh, mesh) {
    purrr::imap_dfr(responses_by_mesh, function(model_status, response) {
      
      keep <- intersect(names(model_status), statuses_type)
      
      purrr::map_dfr(keep, function(status) {
        families <- names(model_status[[status]])
        if (length(families) == 0) return(NULL)
        
        tibble::tibble(region = region,
                       mesh = mesh,
                       response = response,
                       family = families,
                       status = status)
      })
    })
  })
})

sanity_df <- sanity_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(region = factor(region, levels = c("west", "east")))%>%
  dplyr::mutate(mesh = factor(mesh, levels = c("cutoff_3",
                                               "cutoff_5",
                                               "cutoff_7",
                                               "cutoff_10",
                                               "cutoff_15"))) 

ggplot(sanity_df, aes(x = response, y = family, fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(region ~ mesh) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("models_valid" = "#2ca25f",
               "models_fit_failed" = "#de2d26",
               "models_sanity_failed" = "#ffb703"),
    labels = c(
      "models_valid" = "Converged fit",
      "models_fit_failed" = "Non-convergent fit",
      "models_sanity_failed" = "Converged fit rejected after \npost-fit consistency checks")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0.9, "cm"),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.9, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(lineheight = 1.1),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


```


## 3.2. Model parameter estimates

Parameter estimates and confidence intervals are compared across candidate distribution families and spatial mesh configurations. The plots distinguish model components where applicable.
 
```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {
  
params_by_region$west %>%
  mutate(mesh = factor(mesh, levels = c("cutoff_3",
                                        "cutoff_5",
                                        "cutoff_7",
                                        "cutoff_10",
                                        "cutoff_15"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = family, y = estimate, shape = component, color = family)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), size=0.8,
                width = 0, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  facet_grid(response + parameter ~ mesh, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Family",  y = "Estimate", shape = "Component",
    title = "WEST region : sdmTMB parameters estimates") +
  scale_color_manual(values = family_colors)+
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")

}

```

range: distance beyond which two locations can be considered effectively independent (spatial correlation becomes negligible, approximately ~0.13 correlation).  

sigma_O: marginal standard deviation of the spatial random field (omega); it measures the average amplitude of spatial variation that is persistent over time and not explained by the model. Lower values indicate that covariates explain the spatial structure more effectively.  

sigma_E: marginal standard deviation of the spatio-temporal random field (epsilon); it measures the average amplitude of spatial variation that changes over time and is not explained by the model. Lower values indicate that the spatio-temporal structure is already well captured by the other components of the model.

## 3.3. Simulation-based residual diagnostics (DHARMa)

DHARMa diagnostic plots are displayed for each available region–mesh–response–family combination. These diagnostics support the assessment of residual distribution and model adequacy.

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=5, fig.width=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}

# ============================================================================== #
# VISUALISATION OF DHARMa RESIDUAL DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================================== #

for (region in names(dharma_by_region)) {

  for (mesh_name in names(dharma_by_region[[region]])) {

    for (response_name in names(dharma_by_region[[region]][[mesh_name]])) {

      for (family_name in names(dharma_by_region[[region]][[mesh_name]][[response_name]])) {

        # Extract DHARMa residual object
        dharma_res <- dharma_by_region[[region]][[mesh_name]][[response_name]][[family_name]]

        cat("\n\n###", region, " - ", mesh_name, " - ", response_name, " - ", family_name, "\n\n")
        
        # Plot residual diagnostics
        if (inherits(dharma_res, "DHARMa")) {
          plot(dharma_res)
        }
      }
    }
  }
}


```

## 3.5. Repeated random cross-validation

Repeated random cross-validation was used to assess and compare the predictive performance of candidate models across spatial mesh configurations and distribution families.

**Convergence assessment**

Model convergence was evaluated across cross-validation repetitions for each combination of mesh configuration, response variable, and distribution family. The number of converged, non-converged, and missing convergence results is reported, together with the total number of repetitions.

Only model configurations for which **all cross-validation repetitions converged successfully** were retained for the predictive performance comparison.

**Predictive performance comparison**

Predictive performance was assessed using the mean sum of log-likelihood values across cross-validation repetitions. Higher mean log-likelihood values indicate better predictive performance.

For each response variable, the difference from the highest mean log-likelihood was calculated as:

\[
\Delta \overline{\log L}_i =
\max_j\left(\overline{\log L}_j\right)
- \overline{\log L}_i
\]

where \(\overline{\log L}_i\) represents the mean sum of log-likelihood values for model configuration \(i\).

A value of **Δ mean log-likelihood = 0** identifies the best-performing model configuration within each response variable, while larger values indicate lower predictive performance relative to the best-performing configuration.

Results are presented separately for the Western and Eastern English Channel.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {

convergence_summary <- repeated_randomCV_by_region$west$cv_scores %>%
  group_by(mesh, response, family) %>%
  summarise(n_TRUE = sum(all_converged == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_FALSE = sum(all_converged == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_NA = sum(is.na(all_converged)),
            n_total = n(),
            all_converged = all(all_converged %in% TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(region = "west") %>%
  arrange(region, response, mesh, family)

print(convergence_summary, n = Inf)

}
```

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {

  CV_df <- repeated_randomCV_by_region$west$cv_scores %>%
    group_by(mesh, response, family) %>%
    filter(all(all_converged %in% TRUE)) %>%
    summarise(mean_loglik = mean(sum_loglik, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_repeats = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response) %>%
    mutate(delta_loglik = max(mean_loglik) - mean_loglik) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(mesh = factor(mesh, 
                         levels = c("cutoff_3", "cutoff_5", "cutoff_7",
                                    "cutoff_10", "cutoff_15")))

  ggplot(CV_df, aes(x = delta_loglik, 
                    y = mesh, 
                    color = family, shape = family)) +
    geom_point(size = 4) +
    facet_wrap( ~ response) +
    scale_color_manual(values = family_colors) +
    labs(x = "Delta mean sum log-likelihood",
         y = "Mesh resolution",
         color = "Family distribution",
         shape = "Family distribution",
         title = "Western English Channel") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

# 5. Annual biomass indices

Annual biomass indices and their uncertainty intervals are compared across distribution families and mesh configurations. 

```{r biomass_index_east, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {

  index_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_predictions_by_region$west,
                              
    function(mesh_data, mesh) {
      purrr::imap_dfr(mesh_data, function(response_data, response) {
        
        purrr::imap_dfr(response_data, function(model_data, family) {
          
          as.data.frame(model_data$index) %>%
            dplyr::mutate(mesh = mesh,
                          response = response,
                          family = family)
        })
      })
    }) %>%
    dplyr::filter(response == "totalWeightKg") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(mesh = factor(mesh,
                                levels = c("cutoff_3", "cutoff_5", "cutoff_7",
                                           "cutoff_10", "cutoff_15")))

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(index_df, aes(x = year, y = est,
                                     colour = family, fill = family, group = family)) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = family_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = family_colors) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~mesh, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                   axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
                   legend.position = "top") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "West English Channel",
                  x = NULL,
                  y = "Biomass index (kg)",
                  colour = "Distribution family",
                  fill = "Distribution family")

  print(p)
}

```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = family_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = family_colors) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~mesh, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                   axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
                   legend.position = "top") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "East English Channel",
                  x = NULL,
                  y = "Biomass index (kg)",
                  colour = "Distribution family",
                  fill = "Distribution family")

  print(p)
}

```

<br/>

# 6. Spatial predictions of biomass

Maps show predicted biomass for each region, spatial mesh, and distribution family.

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}

plot_prediction_maps_region <- function(prediction_maps, region_name) {

  if (is.null(prediction_maps[[region_name]])) return(NULL)

  for (mesh_name in names(prediction_maps[[region_name]])) {

    for (family in names(prediction_maps[[region_name]][[mesh_name]])) {

      cat("\n\n#####", region_name, " - ", mesh_name, " - ", family, "\n\n")

      print(prediction_maps[[region_name]][[mesh_name]][[family]])

    }
  }
}

if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {
  plot_prediction_maps_region(prediction_maps, "west")
}

if (isTRUE(East_English_Channel)) {
  plot_prediction_maps_region(prediction_maps, "east")
}

```

<br/>

# 7. Prediction uncertainty: coefficient of variation

The coefficient of variation (CV) expresses prediction uncertainty relative to the estimated value. These maps allow uncertainty patterns to be compared across regions, mesh configurations, response variables, and distribution families. Larger CV values indicate greater relative uncertainty.

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}

plot_cv_maps_region <- function(plots_cv_all, region_name) {
  if (is.null(plots_cv_all[[region_name]])) return(NULL)
  for (mesh_name in names(plots_cv_all[[region_name]])) {
    for (response in names(plots_cv_all[[region_name]][[mesh_name]])) {
      for (family in names(plots_cv_all[[region_name]][[mesh_name]][[response]])) {
        cat("\n\n#####", region_name, " - ", mesh_name, " - ", family, "\n\n")
        print(plots_cv_all[[region_name]][[mesh_name]][[response]][[family]])
      }
    }
  }
}
if (isTRUE(West_English_Channel)) {
  plot_cv_maps_region(plots_cv_all, "west")
}

if (isTRUE(East_English_Channel)) {
  plot_cv_maps_region(plots_cv_all, "east")
}
```
